Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: co-tenancy tolerance & SLO follow-up

Thanks again for your time today, Emily — quick recap and a couple of clarifying asks from our side.

Summary (from today's discovery):
- Primary success metric: inference stability for patient-facing features (p95 latency target ~250ms for short prompts, p50 desirable <120ms).
- Throughput: initial bursty traffic pattern (~600 qps peak across a handful of endpoints), steady-state ~150 qps.
- Data security: HIPAA scope for PHI, SOC2 required for procurement.
- Preference: open to Hosted if isolation guarantees meet SLOs; leaning to Dedicated if we need absolute resource separation.

Open clarifying asks for you:
1) How tolerant are you of occasional p95 spikes (e.g., 500-800ms) during daily bursts? Is there an absolute SLA threshold we should avoid?
2) Do you expect any on-prem/VPC-only requirements for certain workflows (e.g., batch redaction jobs)?
3) Who on your side needs to approve a security attestation (SOC2)? We can share our attestation and the runbook for audit logs.

What we'll do next (Redwood side):
- Attach post-call notes and a first-pass SLO matrix for you to review. (See attachments.)
- Ben will outline a short performance POC plan: controlled tail-latency tests, isolation scenarios (noisy neighbor simulation), and recommended mitigation knobs (batching, KV prefix caching, reserved pools).
- I'll send a calendar invite for a technical POC slot next week (30–45m).

Attachments: 20280320-postcall-notes.pdf (summary), slo-matrix-v1.xlsx (our suggested targets & fallbacks).

Thanks — Grace

Subject: Re: Post-call: co-tenancy tolerance & SLO follow-up

Hi Grace — thanks for the recap and the notes. Really helpful. A few answers inline: 

1) p95 tolerance: our product requirement is that patient-facing interactions should not exceed 500ms p95 more than 0.5% of the time in a month. Occasional short spikes are tolerable during deployments, but sustained p95 > 500ms is a showstopper.
2) On-prem: not required for day-one. We do have a compliance team that might later require certain ETL jobs (PHI batch exports) to run in a VPC or air-gapped environment — likely a second-phase ask.
3) SOC2: send it to me; our security lead (cc'd) will triage. I've attached our security questionnaire — it lists the evidence we'll need.

For hosting preference: if Redwood can provide documented isolation guarantees (per-tenant resource reservations, noise containment strategies, and audit/event logs) with an agreed p95 commitment, we can stay on a Hosted plan for the beta. If not, we'll plan for Dedicated capacity for the initial rollout.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Tran
Head of Product, Medsys Health

Emily — thanks for the note and the p95 threshold. A few technical clarifications and a proposed test plan so you can see how Redwood would validate isolation and tail behavior.

Key assumptions from your side we heard today:
- p95 budget: 500ms monthly SLA ceiling (with target substantially lower).
- Traffic mix: short prompts dominate (seq len < 128 tokens) with occasional longer generations (~512).
- Burst pattern is expected but predictable per endpoint.

Mitigation and validation approach we propose:
1) POC topology: two parallel clusters — a reserved Dedicated pool for Medsys traffic (configurable commit) and a seeded shared pool with controlled co-tenants to validate noisy neighbor impact.
2) Tests we'll run:
   - Synthetic tail-latency tests (controlled QPS ramps) targeting p50/p95/p99 across seq lengths.
   - JVM/GPU saturation runs to force contention and observe degradation modes.
   - KV/prefix cache warmup tests to measure cold vs warm latency deltas.
   - Regression tests with and without batching (to show batching tradeoffs for latency vs cost).
3) Observability: we'll provide token-level traces, per-request latency histograms, and GC/GPU utilization dashboards. Audit events for request headers, model version, and region will be exported to your SIEM.
4) SLA handshake: for Hosted, we can commit to an operational SLO (p95 under the agreed target) with an escape hatch — automatic fallback to a pinned Dedicated pool when contention is detected. That fallback is transparent (same API) but priced differently.

Attachments (for the POC plan): test-plan-brief.pdf (outline), slo-matrix-v1.xlsx (updated with technical notes).

Next steps suggested:
- Grace to book a 45m POC engineering slot next Tue or Wed.
- Medsys to confirm a security contact and return the questionnaire; we will share SOC2 report and audit-runbook in the same email.

I'll also include a short cost delta estimate for Dedicated vs Hosted with committed capacity in the follow-up.
